Authority and Competition: Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70 provides Contracting Officers authority to acquire commercial items, technologies, or services through CSOs. The CSO framework is recognized as a competitive procedure under 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102, treating acquired items as commercial with streamlined processes and fixed-price requirements. This CSO is issued on a full and open competitive basis. AoIs issued under this CSO may specify individual competitive environments. 2. PROCEDURES 2.1. Open Period: This CSO is continuously open until 1 February 2036 and may be updated periodically. The Government may extend this period by amendment. 2 2.2. AoIs: This CSO seeks Solution Briefs, Presentations/Pitches, and/or Written Proposals for commercial products, technologies, and services for USTRANSCOM's mission. Two types of AoIs will be utilized under this CSO: General AoIs: Includes general submissions against the AoIs stated in Attachment 1. Submissions are acce

submissions in accordance with Section 4. New AoIs may be introduced at any time during the solicitation period, and companies are encouraged to regularly check www.SAM.gov for updates. 2.3. CSO Process: This process is designed to accommodate a multiple-phased approach as outlined in Sections 3 and 4. Awards may be made using either FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products or Commercial Services, or OT authority. The Government may make no awards, one award, or multiple awards against the AoI. The Government reserves the right to determine that a combination of solutions is necessary to address the problem or meet mission requirements. CSO submission costs will not be reimbursed by the Government unless specifically stated in an AoI. 2.4. Additional Guidelines: Use FAR Part 12 as a guide for contract provisions and clauses, recognizing they are applicable to resultant FAR-based awards. Robbins is currently fabricating MK 51 and MK 52 targets under contract N61331-24-D-0001, awarded 17 May 2022. Fabrication and assembly of the Mk 65 requires specialized tooling, fixtures and processes identical to those used by Robbins under the above contract effort. Robbins Metal Fab is the only contractor currently mobilized and capable of providing the highly specialized skills to perform this effort within the required time frame. The production efforts here in Panama City are derived by Policy & Guidance Reference under OPNAVINST 3110.18 - Navy Target Program and Allocation Process. MCM Mk 65 target capabilities will be used to support Mine Hunting Mine Avoidance, Mine Neutralization and data collection events that directly correlate to Fleet and Research and Development Activities . The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. Please note: Before you can use the postbox you must record your interest in a notice. In the case of a Quick Quote or the second stage of a dual stage procedure you must have been invited by the buyer to submit a response. Postbox Response Workspace All postbox re

entity_geography.text: commercial pricing/discounting practices. DO YOU QUALIFY FOR A VA FSS CONTRACT? To qualify for a VA FSS contract you should: Be able to demonstrate that your firm is responsible. Have $150,000 in annual Commercial sales or $25,000 in annual Government sales. Complete the GSA “Pathway to Success” education seminar. Submit a copy of the certificate of completion with your proposal. Please note that this is only required for new offerors without an existing FSS contract. Meet all the requirements of the solicitation. Be able to fulfill all contract obligations outlined in the solicitation. Contact the VA FSS Help Desk to discuss your firm’s eligibility! IMPORTANT CRITERIA TO CONSIDER Assess Your Competition It is recommended that you identify and assess your competition prior to submitting a proposal. This task can be completed by reviewing the Contract Catalog Search Tool, GSA eLibrary or GSA Advantage. These websites contain information regarding the supplies and services that current VA FSS contractors already offer. Your review of the competition should include: competitor’s pricing, delivery times, warranty terms, services, and any other elements that make their offering distinct when compared to your own. Best Value Determination Schedule buyers award task/delivery orders to FSS

Download the solicitation, including all corresponding documents, and follow the instructions for completion. Read the entire Schedule solicitation thoroughly and respond to all requirements. Make sure all offered line items fall within the scope of the Schedule solicitation. Make sure the company is financially sound. Be ready to negotiate the company’s best offer. Other helpful hints: Obtain a Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) Number Register in the System for Acquisition Management (SAM) database. Vendors must be registered in SAM prior to the award of the Schedule contract (see FAR 52.212-4(t)). Submit all required documents including Manufacturer Letter of Supply and proof of insurance as required. DO YOU QUALIFY FOR A VA FSS CONTRACT? To qualify for a VA FSS contract you should: Be able to demonstrate that your firm is responsible. Have $150,000 in annual Commercial sales or $25,000 in annual Government sales. Complete the GSA “Pathway to Success” education seminar. Submit a copy of the certificate of completion with your proposal. Please note that this is only required for new offerors without an existing FSS contract. Meet all the requirements of the solicitation. Be able to fulfill all contract obligations outlined in the solicitation. Contact the VA FSS Help Desk to discuss your firm’s eligibility! B.4 STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS (SOR) B.4.1 EXIM Mission In meeting EXIM’s vital mission to support American job creation, prosperity, and security through exporting, this requirement supports EXIM. EXIM is an independent federal agency that helps create and maintain U.S. jobs by filling gaps in private export financing at no cost to American taxpayers. EXIM provides a variety of financing mechanisms, including working capital guarantees, export-credit insurance and financing to help foreign buyers purchase U.S. goods and services. More information may be obtained here: https://www.exim.gov/ EXIM’s mission is achieved by EXIM facilitating the export of U.S. goods and services through its direct loan, loan guarantee, and credit insurance programs. EXIM’s charter requires that all authorized transactions demonstrate a reasonable assurance of repayment, which requires a thorough analysis and assessment of the credit risk associated with each transaction. Many EXIM personnel play critical roles in executing EXIM’s mission to have personnel highly capable of analyzing and assessing credit risks.

Authority and Competition: Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70 provides Contracting Officers authority to acquire commercial items, technologies, or services through CSOs. The CSO framework is recognized as a competitive procedure under 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102, treating acquired items as commercial with streamlined processes and fixed-price requirements. This CSO is issued on a full and open competitive basis. AoIs issued under this CSO may specify individual competitive environments. 2. PROCEDURES 2.1. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. To qualify for a VA FSS contract you should: Be able to demonstrate that your firm is responsible. Have $150,000 in annual Commercial sales or $25,000 in annual Government sales. Complete the GSA “Pathway to Success” education seminar. Submit a copy of the certificate of completion with your proposal. Please note that this is only required for new offerors without an existing FSS contract. Meet all the requirements of the solicitation. Be able to fulfill all contract obligations outlined in the solicitation. Contact the VA FSS Help Desk to discuss your firm’s eligibility! IMPORTANT CRITERIA TO CONSIDER Assess Your Competition It is recommended that you identify and assess your competition prior to submitting a proposal. This task can be completed by reviewing the Contract Catalog Search Tool, GSA eLibrary or GSA Advantage. These websites contain information regarding the supplies and services that current VA FSS contractors already offer. Your review of the competition should include: competitor’s pricing, delivery times, warranty terms, services, and any other elements that make their offering distinct when compared to your own. B.4 STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS (SOR) B.4.1 EXIM Mission In meeting EXIM’s vital mission to support American job creation, prosperity, and security through exporting, this requirement supports EXIM. EXIM is an independent federal agency that helps create and maintain U.S. jobs by filling gaps in private export financing at no cost to American taxpayers. EXIM provides a variety of financing mechanisms, including working capital guarantees, export-credit insurance and financing to help foreign buyers purchase U.S. goods and services. More information may be obtained here: https://www.exim.gov/ EXIM’s mission is achieved by EXIM facilitating the export of U.S. goods and services through its direct loan, loan guarantee, and credit insurance programs. EXIM’s charter requires that all authorized transactions demonstrate a reasonable assurance of repayment, which requires a thorough analysis and assessment of the credit risk associated with each transaction. Many EXIM personnel play critical roles in executing EXIM’s mission to have personnel highly capable of analyzing and assessing credit risks.
